vulnerability.category_l2: XML external entity expansion: validateOnParse re-enables DTD processing, so an attacker-supplied XML document can read local files through a file:// entity even when LIBXML_NONET is used

critical_operation.description: addXmlContent() accepts XML from the caller, creates a DOMDocument, sets $dom->validateOnParse = true, and only then calls loadXML($content, $options), where the default options value is LIBXML_NONET. Setting validateOnParse re-enables libxml DTD subset processing, including external entity resolution; LIBXML_NONET prevents network fetches but not file:// entities. XML supplied by an attacker can therefore declare a SYSTEM entity pointing at a local file and have its contents expanded into the parsed document, which the caller can then read through the crawler. The 5.4.52 fix removes the validateOnParse assignment.

entry_point.description: Application code calls addXmlContent() with XML that comes from a request or another untrusted source, or uses BrowserKit HttpBrowser to parse a fetched XML page through the crawler.

trace.description: the caller supplies untrusted XML to addXmlContent(); the default options argument is LIBXML_NONET
validateOnParse is enabled on the DOMDocument, re-enabling DTD and external entity processing
loadXML parses the untrusted content with those options, expanding file:// entities

supports: addXmlContent() has the signature (string $content, string $charset = "UTF-8", int $options = LIBXML_NONET)
it creates a DOMDocument and sets $dom->validateOnParse = true at line 243 before loadXML($content, $options) at line 246
the default LIBXML_NONET therefore does not prevent file:// entity expansion once validateOnParse re-enables DTD processing
at v5.4.52 the addXmlContent() body no longer contains the validateOnParse assignment; loadXML is still called with the caller-supplied options
the file still contains one validateOnParse assignment at line 1184 inside parseXhtml(), which this fix did not touch
the patch removes exactly one line, $dom->validateOnParse = true, from addXmlContent()
the patch adds a regression test in AbstractCrawlerTestCase that feeds XML containing a file:// external entity
the pre-image blob 239ace66 and post-image blob 0f6fb02b match the file contents at v5.4.45 and v5.4.52
the file opens with a PHP open tag and declares namespace Symfony\Component\DomCrawler

source_crosscheck.notes: All sources agree on CWE-611, the validateOnParse mechanism, the <5.4.52 range and the v5.4.52 release, and both the CNA record and the GHSA name the same fix commit eea5fd74 (no dead reference in this advisory). required_before_promotion: An independent reviewer must read Crawler::addXmlContent at v5.4.45 and confirm validateOnParse is set before loadXML with a LIBXML_NONET default.
An independent reviewer must confirm eea5fd74 is absent from v5.4.45 and present in v5.4.52, and that the fix removes only that assignment.
An independent reviewer must confirm the affected range includes 5.4.45 and the fixed release is 5.4.52.
An independent reviewer must record that parseXhtml still sets validateOnParse in v5.4.52 and assess whether that is in scope of this CVE.
No formal reviews.jsonl row may be written until a named independent reviewer returns a verdict.

limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No PHP/libxml runtime or XML payload was executed; the finding is static and the libxml behavior is taken from the advisory and source.
Exploitability requires application code to pass untrusted XML into addXmlContent(); no specific application was tested.
parseXhtml() in the fixed v5.4.52 file still sets validateOnParse before loadHTML(); that residual site is outside the advisory scope but is recorded so it is not mistaken for a complete fix surface.
Only the 5.4 branch was fetched and compared; 6.4.40, 7.4.12 and 8.0.12 were not diffed.
GHSA label LOW disagrees with the 4.0 8.7 and 3.1 7.5 scores.
The GHSA page/OSV label is Low with a divergent vector (PR:L/VC:N/VI:L); it is internally consistent with that vector but inconsistent with the CNA and NVD scores.
open_questions: Whether loadHTML with validateOnParse can expand external entities in the same libxml versions was not tested.
Which caller-supplied XML paths exist in typical Symfony applications was not surveyed.
